kpis.label: Awarded to nine projects recovering scandium, copper, antimony and rare earths from industrial byproducts, on top of an Aug 11 White House announcement of $2B+ in new minerals/magnets/battery investment; sparked a sector-wide rally (Materials +2.09% Aug 21, MP +9.3%, USAR +8%)

Stock ran from ~$38 to $60.16 as a Q2 beat (revenue $108.5M, +89% YoY, NdPr production +51%) was followed by the Aug 18 DOE grant news and a broad critical-minerals sector bid; still down materially over the past year

Pulled back from the Aug 7 all-time high of $6.77/lb on profit-taking; Commerce Secretary Lutnick's Jun 30 deadline to recommend refined-copper tariffs has now lapsed by nearly two months with no announcement, and other reporting points to any phase-in starting no earlier than 2027

Shareholder vote set for Aug 28 remains management's 'final remaining closing condition' with no regulatory hurdles left — shares have recovered +21.7% over the past 30 days despite USAR's own Q2 revenue miss ($5.82M vs. $8.21M est.)

themes.title: Beijing weaponizing processing dominance
themes.description: Ex-China rare-earth prices remain far above pre-controls levels after Beijing's April-2025 move — yttrium oxide near $1,100/kg (~140x), dysprosium oxide ~$1,450/kg, terbium oxide ~$4,500/kg (4-5x) — and shipments of yttrium, dysprosium and terbium into the US remain down roughly 50% versus pre-control levels. China widened controls further in 2026, adding 10 US firms in June and 14 EU firms in July, even as the NdPr alloy benchmark jumped 21.4% in a single month through Jul 1. Trump signed EO 14415 (Jul 20), tightening waivers for defense contractors sourcing from covered nations.

themes.title: Truce getting tested on two clocks
themes.description: The Busan truce (Oct 2025) suspended the Oct 9 export controls for one year and paused gallium/germanium/antimony/superhard dual-use restrictions through Nov 27, 2026, while general rare-earth/battery-material export licenses run through roughly Nov 10, 2026 — two different deadlines Washington and Beijing still need to navigate. China's Jun 22 entity-list additions targeted MP Materials and USA Rare Earth, the two largest recipients of US federal rare-earth investment ($550M and $1.6B), and remain unresolved.

themes.title: Washington's playbook, compounding company by company
themes.description: Project Vault's $10B EXIM loan + ~$2B private capital remains the umbrella policy, reinforced by an Aug 11 White House announcement of $2B+ in new minerals/magnets/battery investment and DOE's Aug 18 award of $162M to nine critical-minerals recovery projects (scandium, copper, antimony, REEs). On top of that, Energy Fuels' ASM implementation and USA Rare Earth's Serra Verde vote both land Aug 28. Separately, Malaysia is weighing an easing of its rare-earth export moratorium and Indonesia resumed exports Aug 3 — early signs of non-China, non-US supply also entering the picture.

rows.angle: Only US rare-earth mine + processing (Mountain Pass); $500M Apple magnet offtake (shipments from 2027) + $400M DoD convertible preferred (DoD now largest shareholder, ~15%)
rows.watch for: Q2 (Aug 6) beat on revenue ($108.5M, +89% YoY) with NdPr production up 51%; stock then ran from ~$38 (Jul 29) to $60.16 (Aug 21, +9.3% that day alone) as the Aug 18 DOE critical-minerals grant news broadened the rally across the sector. 10X plant (2028) still carries DoD's ≥$140M EBITDA guarantee at a $110/kg NdPr price floor; capex guidance reaffirmed at $500–600M

rows.angle: Largest non-China rare-earth producer (Australia/Malaysia); pushing into magnet metals
rows.watch for: FY2026 results and investor briefing land Aug 26 under interim CEO Pol Le Roux — the first full-year report since the leadership change and the A$750M equity raise; still the next real test of the Towards-2030 dilution thesis against the JS Link Malaysia magnet partnership

The lithium-cycle-turning case strengthened for a second straight week: China carbonate spot climbed to CNY152,250/t by Aug 21 (from a 6-month low near CNY140,000 in early August), Q2 beat (EPS $3.75 vs. $3.27 est., energy-storage realized pricing $19.53/kg vs. $12.17/kg a year ago) drove the stock from the low-$130s to $143.25 (Aug 17–21, +11% weekly), and the average analyst target ($173.56) now sits well above Citi's post-earnings cut to $175

rows.angle: Copper — the electrification metal at scale
rows.watch for: Copper pulled back to ~$6.55/lb by Aug 19 (a two-week low) off its Aug 7 record of $6.77/lb as profit-taking set in; Lutnick's Jun 30 deadline to recommend refined-copper tariffs has now lapsed by nearly two months with no announcement, and other reporting suggests any phase-in may not start before 2027. Grasberg ramp and FY26 guidance unchanged, but the policy catalyst just got pushed further out

rows.angle: US rare-earth mine-to-magnet aspirant; Texas mine + Oklahoma magnet plant; DoC $1.6B LOI + ~10% equity stake (Jan 2026, priced $17.17)
rows.watch for: Q2 (Aug 10) missed again — revenue $5.82M vs. $8.21M est., adjusted loss $0.15/share vs. $0.13 est. — but net loss narrowed sharply to $10.33M from $142.51M a year ago, and shares have since rallied +21.7% over 30 days to ~$19.93 as the market looks past the miss toward the Aug 28 Serra Verde vote (no remaining regulatory hurdles, per management) and a new Blacksburg, SC magnet-plant site

rows.angle: Uranium + rare-earth processing at White Mesa
rows.watch for: ASM implementation is locked for Aug 28 (98%+ shareholder approval Aug 12), de-risking one of two simultaneous deals; the $1.9B VAC deal's timeline is newly ambiguous — the Q2 10-Q points to a late-August close while other reporting suggests early 2027. White Mesa uranium processing remains paused for maintenance until Q4 2026/early 2027; ~$1B liquidity

Thacker Pass now at 95%+ detailed engineering and 80%+ procurement, with $1.8B of the $2.93B capex budget spent and 1,600+ workers on site; mechanical completion still targeted late 2027. $1.3B total cash (incl. $530.3M at the JV level) as of Jun 30, but the Aug 6 $175M Yorkville convertible facility remains a relatively expensive layer atop the $2.23B DoE loan

bear_case.title: Commodity cycles cut both ways
bear_case.description: Lithium's turn now has two straight weeks of evidence behind it (China spot up to CNY152,250/t from a 6-month low, Albemarle +11% weekly on its Q2 beat) — but copper already illustrates the flip side: it hit a fresh record ($6.77/lb) on Aug 7 and had pulled back to $6.55/lb by Aug 19. Records don't stay records, and a two-week recovery doesn't yet confirm a durable cycle turn either.

bear_case.title: China can flood the market
bear_case.description: Beijing has both weaponized scarcity (yttrium oxide up ~140x since April 2025) and, historically, dumped supply when it suited its interests. It also widened entity-list controls to 14 EU firms in July even as Malaysia weighs easing its own rare-earth export moratorium and Indonesia resumed exports — alternative non-China supply emerging that could pressure ex-China pricing from the other direction over time.

bear_case.title: Juniors dilute
bear_case.description: USA Rare Earth missed Q2 revenue again ($5.82M vs. $8.21M est.), yet the company is still issuing 126.85M new shares (34.1% of the combined company) to close Serra Verde; Lithium Americas has now spent $1.8B of Thacker Pass's $2.93B capex budget on top of the $175M Yorkville convertible facility layered onto its DoE loan. Building refining capacity remains expensive, and names without direct sovereign grants keep diluting to get there.

bear_case.title: Policy dependency
bear_case.description: Lutnick's copper-tariff recommendation is now nearly two months overdue past its Jun 30 deadline, with any phase-in possibly pushed to 2027 or later; Energy Fuels' $1.9B VAC deal has a newly ambiguous close date; and the Busan truce has two different components expiring on two different dates in November. Multiple policy catalysts the sector is leaning on have all gotten murkier, not clearer, this month.

positions.name: MP Materials
positions.note: Fundamentals genuinely improved — Q2 revenue +89% YoY, NdPr production +51% — but the stock's +58% run since Jul 29 was amplified by a broad, sector-wide Aug 18 DOE grant rather than a company-specific catalyst, so weight is trimmed modestly for valuation extension while staying Core. Also appears in the Robotics sleeve — hold it once, not twice.

positions.name: Lynas Rare Earths
positions.note: FY2026 results (Aug 26) are still the next real test of the Towards-2030 dilution thesis; no fresh Lynas-specific news this week, but sizing picked up a share of the weight vacated by Freeport's move to Watch.

positions.name: Albemarle
positions.note: Promoted from Watch: Q2 beat (EPS $3.75 vs. $3.27 est., revenue beat by ~$125M), energy-storage pricing nearly doubled YoY, and China lithium spot has now recovered for a second straight week (CNY152,250/t vs. a CNY140,000 low in early August); the average analyst target ($173.56) sits well above the current ~$143 price, and even Citi's post-earnings-cut target ($175) implies upside. The cycle-turn thesis is confirmed, not just hoped for.

positions.name: Freeport-McMoRan
positions.note: Moved out of Core: copper already pulled back to $6.55/lb by Aug 19 off its Aug 7 record ($6.77/lb), and Lutnick's Jun 30 deadline to recommend refined-copper tariffs has now lapsed by nearly two months with no announcement — other reporting suggests any phase-in may not start until 2027-28. Real business, but priced for a policy catalyst that just got pushed further out; this is a commodity cycle at an unclear point right now.

positions.name: USA Rare Earth
positions.note: Q2 revenue missed again ($5.82M vs. $8.21M est.), but net loss narrowed sharply to $10.33M from $142.51M YoY, and shares have recovered +21.7% over 30 days to ~$19.93 as the market looks past the miss toward Friday's Aug 28 Serra Verde vote, which management says faces no remaining regulatory hurdles. Sized up slightly to reflect the de-risking, still small given the dilution ahead.

positions.name: Energy Fuels
positions.note: ASM implementation is now locked for Aug 28, real progress on one of two deals — but the $1.9B VAC deal's close date is newly ambiguous (10-Q says late August, other reporting says early 2027), a fresh uncertainty that roughly offsets the ASM progress. Weight held steady.

positions.name: Lithium Americas
positions.note: Thacker Pass hit 95%+ engineering and 80%+ procurement with $1.8B of the $2.93B budget spent and 1,600+ workers on site — steady, expected construction progress, not a new catalyst — while the Aug 6 $175M Yorkville convertible facility remains an expensive layer atop the DoE loan. Sizing unchanged.
